memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"But the hide of the bull and all its flesh, as well as the head and legs, the internal organs and the intestines—that is, all the rest of the bull—he must take outside the camp to a place ceremonially clean, where the ashes are thrown, and burn it there in a wood fire on the ash heap."'" - Lev 4:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Everything else — the hide, the flesh, the head, the legs, all of it — is carried out of the camp and burned on the ash heap.

Nobody eats this one. Unlike the fellowship offering, there is no meal here. The sin offering for the priest ends outside, in the place where refuse goes.

Sin carries the body away from the community. That is the picture. Something has to be removed, taken beyond the boundary, disposed of where the people live and worship.

The writer of Hebrews saw this and made one of the most moving connections in the New Testament. He points out that the bodies of these sin offerings were burned outside the camp, and then says: And so Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy through his own blood (Heb 13:11-12).

Jesus did not die in the temple. He died outside Jerusalem, on a rubbish-strewn hill, in the place of rejection and shame. He was taken out so that we could be brought in.

Hebrews then adds a challenge: let us, then, go to him outside the camp, bearing the disgrace he bore (Heb 13:13). Following Christ sometimes means accepting the outsider's place, as He did.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I understood that Jesus took the place of rejection so that I could be welcomed?
2. Am I willing to be identified with Christ even when it costs me acceptance?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You went outside the gate so that I could come inside. Thank You for bearing the shame that belonged to me, and give me courage to stand with You. Amen.
